dedupe_keys.name: digital earth sweden des national earth observation data platform

description: Digital Earth Sweden (DES) is Sweden's national platform for nationally adapted satellite data, covering Sweden and the Baltic Sea region. It grew from the Rymddatalabb collaboration started in 2019 by AI Sweden, the Swedish National Space Agency, RISE and Luleå University of Technology, inspired by an Australian model, and has been developed since 2021. The platform gathers, quality-assures, processes and makes available Earth observation data, including Copernicus data, with tools for analysis, storage and reproducible work, so that agencies, researchers and others can use it. The Space Agency funds and steers DES and RISE develops and operates it, including data centre capacity, under an agreement that runs to 2027. Data listed as available includes Copernicus, Lantmäteriet, SMHI, the Swedish Agency for Marine and Water Management, the Environmental Protection Agency's national land cover data, MSB and an archive with an Open Data Cube, with openEO training material. The page describes it as open for authorities, researchers and other actors to use; no licence or cost is stated on the page read. Caveats: the page is a description, and access conditions sit on the platform itself. Coverage is Sweden and the Baltic Sea region. It supports hazard exposure and climate adaptation analysis for infrastructure, such as flood and forest change monitoring; related records are Digital Earth Australia and Terrascope.
